notes:
A waiting room served to every URL is no longer judged as the site.

When a site is under load it may answer every request with a short holding page
— "we are experiencing high demand, thank you for your patience" — at HTTP 200,
with a real title. Docket read those as the site's own pages: a fixture of two
dozen produced seventy-two findings about content that was never served.

Two existing guards could not see it. One covers a body with no words at all;
the other catches a short shared body but runs inside duplicate detection, which
skips short pages before it begins. The shortest holding pages fell between them.

They are now recognised, taken out of the judged set, and reported separately so
you can see Docket was not shown those pages. Measured in characters rather than
words, so a language that does not put spaces between them is not mistaken for a
holding page.
